---
name: Release checklist
about: Manual Windows-only verification for promoting a pre-release to a stable tag
title: "Release vX.Y.Z"
labels: release
---

Candidate: (none yet)

Everything here is Windows-only (the supported platform) and manual on
purpose: it is the surface `zig build ci` cannot reach - interactive pickers,
the clipboard, real PATH and registry mutation, the Scoop channels, and the
install as it exists on a machine that has been running an older version.

The stable tag will not publish until every box below is checked. The
`Candidate:` line above is written by CI when a pre-release tag is pushed;
verify against THAT build, and if a new pre goes out, start again from the
build the line names.

**Sandboxing:** steps marked 🧪 must run against a scratch store, never the
real one. In a fresh PowerShell:

```powershell
$env:NIX_HOME = "$env:TEMP\nix-rc"        # scratch store for this shell only
```

Steps touching the **real** `~/.nix` are marked ⚠️ - snapshot first:

```powershell
Copy-Item ~/.nix ~/.nix-pre-release-backup -Recurse
```

---

## 1. Install and upgrade path

- [ ] Download the candidate zip from its GitHub release; `nix.exe --version`
      prints the candidate tag (baked from the tag, not `0.0.0`).
- [ ] ⚠️ Deploy over the daily install (`r nix :build` + `r nix :sync`, or
      drop-in + `nix --sync`); existing aliases, groups, actions, `[shortcuts]`,
      notes and `[bin]` exports all still resolve.
- [ ] Any upgrade step this release needs from an older version is written
      down for the release notes (section 12).

## 2. `--init`, PATH and the registry

- [ ] 🧪 `nix --init` completes in a scratch shell; **`$PROFILE` is untouched**
      (compare hash and timestamp before and after).
- [ ] 🧪 `~/.nix/bin` (scratch) is on the *user* PATH in the registry
      (`Get-ItemProperty HKCU:\Environment -Name Path`). **Clean the scratch
      entry up afterwards** - type-preserving, no `setx`:

      ```powershell
      $bin = "$env:TEMP\nix-rc\bin"
      $k = Get-Item HKCU:\Environment
      $raw = $k.GetValue('Path','','DoNotExpandEnvironmentNames')
      $new = ($raw -split ';' | Where-Object { $_ -ne $bin }) -join ';'
      Set-ItemProperty HKCU:\Environment -Name Path -Value $new -Type $k.GetValueKind('Path')
      ```

- [ ] 🧪 Every wrapper exe exists after init: `o e s y p r sg ff nix`.
- [ ] 🧪 `~/.nix/AGENTS.md` is regenerated by `--init` and by `--sync`.
- [ ] A brand-new terminal (not a refreshed one) picks up PATH; `o` and `r` work.

## 3. Wrappers and `[shortcuts]`

- [ ] 🧪 Add a rename (e.g. `sg = "g"` - the KEY is the builtin slot, the value
      is the new name), `nix --sync`: the new wrapper appears and dispatches by
      argv0. Reversing it (`g = "sg"`) names no builtin slot, so it is silently
      ignored and nothing happens - that is the config being wrong, not `--sync`.
- [ ] 🧪 Rename again: the **old** wrapper exe is deleted (custom-to-custom
      included).
- [ ] 🧪 An invalid shortcut name leaves the builtin working and installs
      nothing.
- [ ] ⚠️ `--sync` while a wrapper is running (a live `r <alias> <long-cmd>`)
      completes; the running session is unaffected and no half-written exe is
      left behind.

## 4. Pickers and the clipboard

- [ ] `o <alias>` with no argument, `o +<group>`, `nix --prune`, `nix --actions`
      and `nix --notes` each open fzf and act on the pick.
- [ ] `ff <alias> <pat>` and `s <alias> <pat>` return results and open the picks.
- [ ] `y <alias>` copies the path; `y <alias> <pat>` puts the real FILES on the
      clipboard (paste into Explorer, not just a text field).
- [ ] `p <alias>` saves clipboard text, and an image, into the alias dir.
- [ ] With Everything running, doctor's `es` probe passes; stop Everything and
      it reports the fallback instead of passing falsely.

## 5. Groups

- [ ] `r +<group> <cmd>` fans out in each member dir, labelled per member.
- [ ] `s`/`y` `+<group> <pat>` show `alias\rel` rows; picks open or copy.
- [ ] `p +<group>` pastes into the picked member.
- [ ] 🧪 A malformed group token errors and does **not** fall through to a
      picker. Run on a REAL console - an agent shell refuses pickers anyway, so
      failing there proves nothing. Each exits non-zero, prints the message
      below, and opens NO picker:
      - `o +` / `y pa+` -> `nix: invalid group token "..." (EmptyGroupName)`
      - `r +nosuch echo hi` -> `nix: unknown group "+nosuch"`

      The failure being guarded: an unknown PLAIN alias deliberately hands off
      to the directory picker to register it on the fly (resolve.zig). A bad
      `+token` treated as an ordinary alias name lands in that same path, so
      instead of an error you get a menu offering to register `+` as an alias -
      and in `r +<group> <cmd>` a fan-out could quietly run the command
      somewhere it was never aimed at. Control: `o nosuchalias` SHOULD open the
      picker. If all three print `unknown alias`, the group namespace is not
      failing closed.

## 6. Actions, provenance and secrets

- [ ] 🧪 A freshly cloned project's `.nix/actions.toml` asks before its first
      run, and refuses (does not hang) with no console.
- [ ] 🧪 `nix --trust <alias>` approves it; editing the file asks again.
- [ ] An action beginning with `sudo` raises the UAC prompt and runs elevated
      in its own console.
- [ ] `${secret:NAME}` resolves from Credential Manager, and the value does
      **not** appear in the elevated command line or in any log.
- [ ] `r <alias> --deps :build` runs dependencies first and stops at the first
      failure.

## 7. Per-project environment

- [ ] ⚠️ `.nix/env.toml` variables reach a real `r` command, and `nix <alias>
      --env` shows their provenance.
- [ ] Variables do not leak between members of a group fan-out or a `--deps`
      chain.

## 8. `[bin]` exports

- [ ] `nix --sync-bin` installs a project's export into `~/.nix/bin`; the name
      runs from any directory.
- [ ] A rebuilt binary asks for consent again; a tampered or no-longer-declared
      export is reported by `nix --doctor`.

## 9. `[notify]` hooks

- [ ] `on_finish`, `on_paste` and `on_yank` fire against the real notifier, with
      quoting intact.

## 10. Doctor and notes on the real machine

- [ ] ⚠️ `nix --doctor` is green; `-q` shows only problems; `--json` parses.
- [ ] ⚠️ `nix <alias> --note <text>` appends, and `nix --notes <pat>` finds it.

## 11. Backup and rollback

- [ ] ⚠️ `nix --export backup.toml` against the real store; stash it with the
      `~/.nix` snapshot. This is the rollback artifact for this release.
- [ ] 🧪 `--import` merges without overwriting, and `--import --replace`
      restores exactly.

## 12. Release hygiene

- [ ] Release CI is green on the candidate tag.
- [ ] The pre-release is marked **Pre-release** on GitHub and is not "Latest"
      (Excavator's checkver reads `/releases/latest`).
- [ ] The stable Scoop bucket has **not** moved to the pre.
- [ ] `scoop update nix-nightly` still works.
- [ ] Release notes lead with an **Upgrading** section if anything breaks.

## 13. Promote

- [ ] `git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "..." && git push origin vX.Y.Z` (the same commit
      as the candidate unless fixes landed - if they did, cut a new pre and
      re-verify from section 1).
- [ ] The release publishes as **Latest**.
- [ ] Excavator bumps the stable bucket. Do not hand-edit it.
- [ ] `scoop update nix` on the daily machine; `nix --version` matches the tag.

CI closes this issue and copies the completed checklist into the release notes
once the stable tag publishes. Nothing to delete by hand.
